recipes.name: Blank
recipes.summary: Empty starter recipe. One field, one no-op stage. Replace contents of pipelineDsl with your own simulation.

recipes.name: FitzHugh-Nagumo (example)
recipes.summary: Excitable medium. Fast u spikes through a cubic threshold; slow v recovers and suppresses. Diffusion turns spikes into traveling fronts; an asymmetric seed breaks a front into a rotating spiral.

recipes.name: Belousov-Zhabotinsky (example)
recipes.summary: 3-field oscillating chemistry. u is the fast autocatalyst, v is the medium-timescale inhibitor, w is the slow tertiary recovery. Three timescales produce nested target waves and rotating spirals.

recipes.name: Kuramoto chimera (example)
recipes.summary: Coupled phase oscillators on a sphere. Sakaguchi lag α near π/2 lets sync and chaos coexist; the sphere's closed surface produces rotating-spiral chimera patterns.

recipes.name: Ice-albedo (example)
recipes.summary: Bistable climate. Ice reflects sunlight and stays cold; ocean absorbs it and stays warm. Two stable basins; a perturbation near the threshold can flip the entire planet.

recipes.name: SIR epidemic (example)
recipes.summary: Spatial Susceptible-Infected-Recovered model. Outbreak fronts propagate from seed points and leave a recovered trail behind them; β/γ controls wave speed and final attack rate.

recipes.name: Klausmeier vegetation (example)
recipes.summary: Semi-arid biomass-water dynamics. Vegetation self-organizes into stripes perpendicular to the slope (Sahelian tiger bush). Drop FLOW SPEED to zero and the same kinetics produce Turing spots.

recipes.name: Predator-prey (example)
recipes.summary: Rosenzweig-MacArthur with diffusion. Prey colonizes empty cells, predators follow eating, a void trails the predators which is then re-colonized. Sustained chase-wave limit cycle.

recipes.name: Wave equation (example)
recipes.summary: Hyperbolic wave on a sphere — leapfrog second-order time integration via history fields. Drop a stone, watch the ripple bounce around the sphere forever (γ=0) or decay smoothly (γ>0).
